MAJOR: `PF_BACKLOG_DB_SCOPES` is the operative safety gate but is unregistered in `config/env-flags.json` (no default/purpose/owner) and absent from `.env.example`; AC-1 requires config/docs consistency and env-flags.json is the declared flag registry.

Scope allowlist is duplicated with divergent normalization: `core/backlog.py` compares via `_norm_scope`, `core/id_allocator.py` via `strip().lower()`, each hardcoding its own `"product_forge,ProductForge-Dashboard"` default — a scope can be DB-authoritative for items but file-authoritative for IDs, silently splitting ID authority.

Diff shows no pinning of `PF_BACKLOG_DB=off` in `structure.yml`/`full-sweep.yml` (both in scope, unchanged); with the default now on, existing file-mode suites reaching backlog code will attempt the HTTP path with a 30s timeout.

`_load_all_from_db` fetches the entire backlog in one `limit=100000` request with no pagination or caching on every read entrypoint; payload, memory and latency grow with tenant item count, undermining the p95 no-regression requirement.

`backlog_db_bench.py` times only `SELECT data ... WHERE tenant_id=%s AND id=%s` for the T1 figure, omitting the `requireTenant` round-trip the design mandates "in the boundary"; it also compares DB (all tenants) against root-only file items, so the evidence does not back the AC-1 performance claim.

AC-3 GP parity is unproven in CI: the pinned workflow contract asserts only `backlog_db_parity.py --tenant product_forge`; no diff line shows a parity run for the generated-product tenant (`ProductForge-Dashboard`).

`backlog_db_backfill.py` ignores `PF_BACKLOG_DB_SCOPES`: it forces mode on and walks every tenant on disk, so it either writes DB rows for tenants still file-authoritative, or (if the mirror honours `_db_for`) reports `ok=N` while writing nothing — untested in both directions.
MINOR: `_load_all_from_db` maps every `HTTPError` (including 500/503) to `BACKLOG_DB_AUTH`, so genuine outages and tenant-context 503s are misfiled as auth failures.

`Put` returns `ErrTenantConflict` when `app.tenant_id != it.TenantID`, surfacing as 409 "conflicts with another tenant" — wrong reason code/status for a context mismatch against the declared taxonomy (`TENANT_CONTEXT_MISSING`, 503).
`precheck.py` uses `os.environ.setdefault("PF_BACKLOG_DB","off")`, which is a no-op once an operator exports the now-default `on`, so precheck silently leaves file mode.
`Authority()` requires migrations 16,18,19,20,21 but not 22; a DB migrated only through 0021 passes the startup gate with the traceability index missing, so cascaded deletes table-scan.
No test asserts that on-mode does *not* write file projections; only the off-mode file write is covered, so the "no file-authoritative writes in on mode" guardrail is unverified.
`backlog_db_export.py` write/skip/overwrite logic is untested (only `target_dir`), and AC-5 evidence exercises `--dry-run` only.
`requireTenant`'s returned tenant is discarded in `Get`/`List`/`Delete`, forcing a second `current_setting` evaluation and an extra round-trip per call; `rows.Err()` is never checked.
Rollback docs order export → parity → `off` with no quiesce/drain step, so writes between export and the flag flip are lost from the file projection.
NIT: `time.sleep(0.12)` is a hardcoded throttle, not the tenant/global RPM backpressure the design claims; no 429 handling or resume marker.
`backlog_db_export.py target_dir()` interpolates the CLI tenant into a filesystem path with no traversal guard.
`PF_BACKUP_CONFIRMED=1` is self-attestation with no binding to an actual verified backup artifact or timestamp.
`backlog_db_backfill.py` silently skips files lacking an `id` without counting them as failures.
SUMMARY: Direction is correct and the prior blockers (workflow mirror, product parity scan, List tenant guard) are genuinely addressed; the cutover logic, fail-closed mapping and migration pair are coherent.
Remaining risks are concentrated in configuration as code: the new scope allowlist is registered nowhere, resolved twice with different normalization, and not proven against CI file-mode suites.
Performance evidence does not measure the boundary it claims, and backfill/parity for the generated-product tenant is asserted rather than demonstrated.
Overall: not releasable as-is; the scope-allowlist single-source and CI off-pinning items should be closed before flipping the default.
